    54→│   │   │   ├── model/__value                      # "claude-opus-4-6[1m]"
    55→│   │   │   └── provider/__value                   # "anthropic"
    56→│   │   ├── prompt/__value                         # user prompt(s)

# gmeta POC Plan

## Context

gmeta is a proposed standard for attaching arbitrary metadata to Git projects, designed by Scott Chacon (GitButler). It defines a tree layout spec for serializing `(target, key, value)` tuples into Git trees on `refs/meta/local/main`, exchangeable over standard Git protocol.

Entire's `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is functionally equivalent to jj's `change-id` — a stable identifier embedded in the commit message that survives rebase/cherry-pick. This maps directly to gmeta's `change-id` target type, meaning checkpoint metadata keyed to `change-id:<checkpoint-id>` survives rewrites without any additional tooling.

Reference implementation: `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/gmeta`
Spec: `gmeta/spec/README.md`

## Goal

Write Entire checkpoint metadata in gmeta exchange format alongside v1/v2, proving interop by reading it back with the Rust `gmeta` CLI.

## Architecture

No go-git changes needed. gmeta is just a tree layout convention — Entire already has all the plumbing:
- `BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateBlobFromContent`, `CreateCommit` in `checkpoint/`
- `V2GitStore` as prior art for a second store struct composing `GitStore`
- Dual-write pattern already exists in `manual_commit_condensation.go`

## Tree Layout Mapping

### Fanout Rule

Per gmeta spec (`spec/exchange-format/exchange.md`), `change-id` targets use: **first 2 hex chars of SHA-1(target-value)**.

So for checkpoint ID `a3b2c4d5e6f7`: fanout = `sha1("a3b2c4d5e6f7")[:2]`.

This is NOT the same as `checkpoint-id[:2]`. The fanout is derived from a hash of the value, not the value itself.

### Per-Session Encoding

A checkpoint can contain multiple sessions (concurrent agents, `entire attach`). gmeta has no native session concept, so we namespace per session under the checkpoint's change-id target:

```
change-id/<fanout>/<checkpoint-id>/
├── entire/
│   ├── strategy/__value                           # "manual-commit"
│   ├── cli-version/__value                        # CLI version
│   ├── branch/__value                             # branch name
│   ├── checkpoints-count/__value                  # total across all sessions
│   └── files-touched/__set/                       # merged from all sessions
│       ├── <sha1(value)[:10]>                     # "src/foo.go"
│       └── <sha1(value)[:10]>                     # "src/bar.go"
├── session/
│   ├── ids/__list/                                # ordered session IDs
│   │   ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>                    # "2026-01-13-uuid1"
│   │   └── <timestamp>-<hash5>                    # "2026-01-13-uuid2"
│   ├── <session-id-1>/
│   │   ├── agent/
│   │   │   ├── name/__value                       # "Claude Code"
│   │   │   ├── model/__value                      # "claude-opus-4-6[1m]"
│   │   │   └── provider/__value                   # "anthropic"
│   │   ├── prompt/__value                         # user prompt(s)
│   │   └── transcript/__list/                     # chunked JSONL entries
│   │       ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>
│   │       └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
│   └── <session-id-2>/
│       ├── agent/
│       │   ├── name/__value
│       │   ├── model/__value
│       │   └── provider/__value
│       ├── prompt/__value
│       └── transcript/__list/
│           └── ...
```

This means:
- Checkpoint-level fields (`strategy`, `branch`, `files-touched`) live at the top level
- Each session gets its own subtree under `session/<session-id>/`
- `session/ids` is a list preserving session ordering
- Adding a session (via `entire attach` or concurrent agent) appends to `session/ids` and creates a new `session/<id>/` subtree — no overwrites

### Single-Session Shorthand

When there is exactly one session, the layout is identical — just one `session/<id>/` subtree. No special-casing needed.

## Security: Redaction

All data written to `refs/meta/local/main` MUST be redacted before creating git blobs, matching v1/v2 behavior:

- Transcripts: pass through `redact.JSONLBytes()` before chunking into list entries
- Prompts: pass through `redact.String()` before writing `__value` blob
- File paths in `files-touched`: no redaction needed (already public via git history)

This is a hard requirement, not an implementation detail. The gmeta ref is permanent and pushable.

## Write Paths

`GmetaStore` must be wired into **all** paths that write committed checkpoints, not just condensation:

| Write path | File | When | Task checkpoints |
|---|---|---|---|
| Condensation | `manual_commit_condensation.go` | PostCommit hook — session data condensed on user commit | Full support |
| Stop finalization | `manual_commit_hooks.go` | Stop hook — transcript/prompts replaced with final versions | Full support |
| Attach | `attach.go` | `entire attach` — adds external session data to existing checkpoint | Full support |
| Migrate | `migrate.go` | `entire migrate` — copies v1 checkpoints to v2 (and now gmeta) | **Session data only** |

**Migrate and task checkpoints**: Migration copies task metadata from v1 to v2 via raw tree splicing (`copyTaskMetadataToV2`), not through `WriteCommittedOptions` — the opts only carry `IsTask` and `ToolUseID`, not `AgentID`, `CheckpointUUID`, subagent transcript content, or incremental payloads. Building a v1-tree-walker that re-extracts all task fields into gmeta format is not worth the complexity for a one-time operation. The gmeta migrate path writes session-level data only; task metadata remains available in v1 and v2.

### Task Checkpoint Encoding

Task checkpoints (subagent work) are written under `session/<session-id>/task/<tool-use-id>/`:

```
session/<session-id>/task/<tool-use-id>/
├── agent-id/__value                              # subagent identifier (opts.AgentID)
├── checkpoint-uuid/__value                       # UUID for transcript truncation on rewind (opts.CheckpointUUID)
├── transcript/__list/                            # subagent transcript (chunked, from opts.SubagentTranscriptPath)
│   ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>
│   └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
└── incremental/__list/                           # incremental checkpoints (ordered)
    ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>                       # JSON: {type, tool_use_id, data}
    └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
```

These fields map 1:1 to what `WriteCommittedOptions` already carries: `AgentID`, `CheckpointUUID`, `SubagentTranscriptPath`, and `IncrementalData`/`IncrementalType`/`IncrementalSequence`. No new plumbing needed.

**Final task checkpoints** write `agent-id`, `checkpoint-uuid`, and `transcript` entries.

**Incremental task checkpoints** (`opts.IsIncremental`) append to `incremental/__list/`. Each entry is a JSON blob with `{type, tool_use_id, timestamp, data}` — same content as v1's `checkpoints/NNN-<tool-use-id>.json` but as a gmeta list entry instead of numbered files.

Redaction applies to both: subagent transcripts via `redact.JSONLBytes()` (falling back to `redact.Bytes()`), incremental data via `redact.JSONLBytes()`.

### Write API

```go
type GmetaStore struct {
    repo *git.Repository
    gs   *GitStore
}

// WriteCommitted writes or appends a session to a checkpoint in gmeta format.
// If the checkpoint already exists, the new session is added alongside existing ones.
// Handles both session and task checkpoints (including incremental).
func (s *GmetaStore) WriteCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts WriteCommittedOptions) error

// UpdateCommitted replaces transcript and prompts for an existing session.
// Used at stop time to finalize with complete session data.
// Replaces the transcript list entries and prompt value for the given session.
func (s *GmetaStore) UpdateCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts UpdateCommittedOptions) error
```

Both methods required from day one. `UpdateCommitted` replaces the `session/<id>/transcript/__list/` entries and `session/<id>/prompt/__value` blob for the target session. This matches the replace semantics v1/v2 already use — gmeta lists are append-only in the *exchange* model, but within a single serialization we control the full tree, so replacing entries before push is fine.

### Wiring Pattern

Same as v2 — non-fatal wrapper so gmeta failures don't break existing flow:

```go
gmetaStore := cpkg.NewGmetaStore(repo)
if err := gmetaStore.WriteCommitted(ctx, opts); err != nil {
    logging.Warn(ctx, "gmeta write failed", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
}
```

Applied in all four write paths above.

## Steps

### Step 1: GmetaStore struct + WriteCommitted + UpdateCommitted

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go`

Implementation details:
- String values: blob at `<key-path>/__value`
- List values: blobs at `<key-path>/__list/<timestamp-ms>-<hash5>`
- Set values: blobs at `<key-path>/__set/<sha1-of-value[:10]>` containing the value
- Target base path: `change-id/<sha1(checkpoint-id)[:2]>/<checkpoint-id>/`
- Ref: `refs/meta/local/main`
- Redaction: `redact.JSONLBytes()` for transcripts, `redact.String()` for prompts
- Multi-session: read existing tree, find/create `session/<id>/` subtree

Reuses from `GitStore`: `BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateBlobFromContent`, `CreateCommit`

### Step 2: Wire into all write paths

Add `GmetaStore` calls to condensation, stop finalization, attach, and migrate. Non-fatal in all paths.

### Step 3: Validate interop

Install the Rust gmeta CLI, point at a repo with Entire checkpoints:

```bash
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:agent:model
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:prompt
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:transcript
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> entire:files-touched
```

Verify data round-trips correctly.

## Open Questions

- **Token usage / attribution**: Entire-specific structured data. Options:
  - Namespace as individual keys: `session/<id>/entire:token-usage:input/__value`, etc.
  - Or store as JSON string under `session/<id>/entire:token-usage/__value`
  - Decision: defer to after POC, not needed for interop validation
- **Push/fetch**: gmeta uses `refs/meta/local/main` for push, `refs/meta/remotes/main` for fetch. Need to decide if this coexists with or replaces v2's push mechanism. Likely coexists for now.
- **Read-side**: Not needed for POC. Future work to have `entire session list/show` read from gmeta format.
- **Task checkpoints**: Included. Final tasks write `agent-id`, `checkpoint-uuid`, `transcript` under `session/<id>/task/<tool-use-id>/`. Incremental tasks append to `incremental/__list/`. Open question: should the gmeta Rust CLI understand these Entire-specific task keys, or are they opaque vendor-namespaced data?

## Estimated Scope

~300-400 lines for `GmetaStore` (write + update + multi-session handling + redaction), ~20 lines to wire into all four write paths. Tests + interop validation on top.

    40→// WriteCommitted writes a committed checkpoint to the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.
    41→// Checkpoints are stored at sharded paths: <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/
    42→//
    43→// For task checkpoints (IsTask=true), additional files are written under tasks/<tool-use-id>/:
    44→//   - For incremental checkpoints: checkpoints/NNN-<tool-use-id>.json
    45→//   - For final checkpoints: checkpoint.json and agent-<agent-id>.jsonl
    46→func (s *GitStore) WriteCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts WriteCommittedOptions) error {
    47→	// Validate identifiers to prevent path traversal and malformed data
    48→	if opts.CheckpointID.IsEmpty() {
    49→		return errors.New("invalid checkpoint options: checkpoint ID is required")
    50→	}
    51→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(opts.SessionID); err != nil {
    52→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid checkpoint options: %w", err)
    53→	}
    54→	if err := validation.ValidateToolUseID(opts.ToolUseID); err != nil {
    55→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid checkpoint options: %w", err)
    56→	}
    57→	if err := validation.ValidateAgentID(opts.AgentID); err != nil {
    58→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid checkpoint options: %w", err)
    59→	}
    60→
    61→	// Ensure sessions branch exists
    62→	if err := s.ensureSessionsBranch(); err != nil {
    63→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to ensure sessions branch: %w", err)
    64→	}
    65→
    66→	// Get branch ref and root tree hash (O(1), no flatten)
    67→	parentHash, rootTreeHash, err := s.getSessionsBranchRef()
    68→	if err != nil {
    69→		return err
    70→	}
    71→
    72→	// Use sharded path: <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/
    73→	basePath := opts.CheckpointID.Path() + "/"
    74→	checkpointPath := opts.CheckpointID.Path()
    75→
    76→	// Flatten only the checkpoint subtree (O(files in checkpoint))
    77→	entries, err := s.flattenCheckpointEntries(rootTreeHash, checkpointPath)
    78→	if err != nil {
    79→		return err
    80→	}
    81→
    82→	// Track task metadata path for commit trailer
    83→	var taskMetadataPath string
    84→
    85→	// Handle task checkpoints
    86→	if opts.IsTask && opts.ToolUseID != "" {
    87→		taskMetadataPath, err = s.writeTaskCheckpointEntries(ctx, opts, basePath, entries)
    88→		if err != nil {
    89→			return err
    90→		}
    91→	}
    92→
    93→	// Write standard checkpoint entries (transcript, prompts, context, metadata)
    94→	if err := s.writeStandardCheckpointEntries(ctx, opts, basePath, entries); err != nil {
    95→		return err
    96→	}
    97→
    98→	// Build checkpoint subtree and splice into root (O(depth) tree surgery)
    99→	newTreeHash, err := s.spliceCheckpointSubtree(rootTreeHash, opts.CheckpointID, basePath, entries)
   100→	if err != nil {
   101→		return err
   102→	}
   103→
   104→	commitMsg := s.buildCommitMessage(opts, taskMetadataPath)
   105→	newCommitHash, err := s.createCommit(newTreeHash, parentHash, commitMsg, opts.AuthorName, opts.AuthorEmail)
   106→	if err != nil {
   107→		return err
   108→	}
   109→
   110→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   111→	newRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, newCommitHash)
   112→	if err := s.repo.Storer.SetReference(newRef); err != nil {
   113→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to set branch reference: %w", err)
   114→	}
   115→
   116→	return nil
   117→}
   118→
   119→// flattenCheckpointEntries reads only the entries under a specific checkpoint path
   120→// from the sessions branch tree. This is O(files in checkpoint) instead of O(all checkpoints).
   121→// Returns an empty map if the checkpoint doesn't exist yet.
   122→func (s *GitStore) flattenCheckpointEntries(rootTreeHash plumbing.Hash, checkpointPath string) (map[string]object.TreeEntry, error) {
   123→	entries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
   124→	if rootTreeHash == plumbing.ZeroHash {
   125→		return entries, nil
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	rootTree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(rootTreeHash)
   129→	if err != nil {
   130→		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrObjectNotFound) {
   131→			return entries, nil // Tree doesn't exist yet
   132→		}
   133→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read root tree %s: %w", rootTreeHash, err)
   134→	}
   135→
   136→	subtree, err := rootTree.Tree(checkpointPath)
   137→	if err != nil {
   138→		return entries, nil //nolint:nilerr // Checkpoint doesn't exist yet
   139→	}
   140→
   141→	// Flatten just this subtree with the full path prefix
   142→	if err := FlattenTree(s.repo, subtree, checkpointPath, entries); err != nil {
   143→		return nil, err
   144→	}
   145→	return entries, nil
   146→}
   147→
   148→// spliceCheckpointSubtree builds a tree from checkpoint-local entries and installs it
   149→// at the correct shard location in the root tree using O(depth) tree surgery.
   150→// basePath is like "a3/b2c4d5e6f7/" (with trailing slash).
   151→// Returns the new root tree hash.
   152→func (s *GitStore) spliceCheckpointSubtree(rootTreeHash plumbing.Hash, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, basePath string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   153→	// Convert entries to relative paths (strip basePath prefix)
   154→	relEntries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry, len(entries))
   155→	for path, entry := range entries {
   156→		relPath := strings.TrimPrefix(path, basePath)
   157→		if relPath == path {
   158→			continue // Entry doesn't have the expected prefix
   159→		}
   160→		relEntries[relPath] = entry
   161→	}
   162→
   163→	// Build the checkpoint subtree from relative entries
   164→	checkpointTreeHash, err := BuildTreeFromEntries(s.repo, relEntries)
   165→	if err != nil {
   166→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to build checkpoint subtree: %w", err)
   167→	}
   168→
   169→	// Splice into root tree at the shard path using tree surgery
   170→	// Path: ["a3"] with entry "b2c4d5e6f7" pointing to the checkpoint tree
   171→	shardPrefix := string(checkpointID[:2])
   172→	shardSuffix := string(checkpointID[2:])
   173→	return UpdateSubtree(s.repo, rootTreeHash, []string{shardPrefix}, []object.TreeEntry{
   174→		{Name: shardSuffix, Mode: filemode.Dir, Hash: checkpointTreeHash},
   175→	}, UpdateSubtreeOptions{MergeMode: MergeKeepExisting})
   176→}

   190→	incData, err := redact.JSONLBytes(opts.IncrementalData)
   191→	if err != nil {
   192→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to redact incremental checkpoint: %w", err)
   193→	}
   194→	checkpoint := incrementalCheckpointData{
   195→		Type:      opts.IncrementalType,
   196→		ToolUseID: opts.ToolUseID,
   197→		Timestamp: time.Now().UTC(),
   198→		Data:      incData,
   199→	}
   200→	cpData, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(checkpoint, "", "  ")

   977→// BuildTreeFromEntries builds a proper git tree structure from flattened file entries.
   978→// Exported for use by strategy package (push_common.go, session_test.go)
   979→func BuildTreeFromEntries(repo *git.Repository, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   980→	// Build a tree structure
   981→	root := &treeNode{
   982→		entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
   983→		files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
   984→	}
   985→
   986→	// Insert all entries into the tree structure
   987→	for fullPath, entry := range entries {
   988→		parts := strings.Split(fullPath, "/")
   989→		insertIntoTree(root, parts, entry)
   990→	}
   991→
   992→	// Recursively build tree objects from bottom up
   993→	return buildTreeObject(repo, root)
   994→}

   996→// insertIntoTree inserts a file entry into the tree structure.
   997→func insertIntoTree(node *treeNode, pathParts []string, entry object.TreeEntry) {
   998→	if len(pathParts) == 1 {
   999→		// This is a file in the current directory
  1000→		node.files = append(node.files, object.TreeEntry{
  1001→			Name: pathParts[0],
  1002→			Mode: entry.Mode,
  1003→			Hash: entry.Hash,
  1004→		})
  1005→		return
  1006→	}
  1007→
  1008→	// This is in a subdirectory
  1009→	dirName := pathParts[0]
  1010→	if node.entries[dirName] == nil {
  1011→		node.entries[dirName] = &treeNode{
  1012→			entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
  1013→			files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
  1014→		}
  1015→	}
  1016→	insertIntoTree(node.entries[dirName], pathParts[1:], entry)
  1017→}

  1019→// buildTreeObject recursively builds tree objects from a treeNode.
  1020→func buildTreeObject(repo *git.Repository, node *treeNode) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
  1021→	var treeEntries []object.TreeEntry
  1022→
  1023→	// Add files
  1024→	treeEntries = append(treeEntries, node.files...)
  1025→
  1026→	// Recursively build subtrees
  1027→	for name, subnode := range node.entries {
  1028→		subHash, err := buildTreeObject(repo, subnode)
  1029→		if err != nil {
  1030→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
  1031→		}
  1032→		treeEntries = append(treeEntries, object.TreeEntry{
  1033→			Name: name,
  1034→			Mode: filemode.Dir,
  1035→			Hash: subHash,
  1036→		})
  1037→	}
  1038→
  1039→	// Sort entries (git requires sorted entries)
  1040→	sortTreeEntries(treeEntries)
  1041→
  1042→	// Create tree object
  1043→	tree := &object.Tree{Entries: treeEntries}
  1044→
  1045→	obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
  1046→	if err := tree.Encode(obj); err != nil {
  1047→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode tree: %w", err)
  1048→	}
  1049→
  1050→	hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
  1051→	if err != nil {
  1052→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to store tree: %w", err)
  1053→	}
  1054→
  1055→	return hash, nil
  1056→}

  1058→// sortTreeEntries sorts tree entries in git's required order.
  1059→// Git sorts tree entries by name, with directories having a trailing /
  1060→func sortTreeEntries(entries []object.TreeEntry) {
  1061→	sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
  1062→		nameI := entries[i].Name

    15→// migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded checks if HEAD has changed since the session started
    16→// and migrates the shadow branch to the new base commit if needed.
    17→//
    18→// This handles the scenario where Claude performs a rebase, pull, or other git operation
    19→// that changes HEAD mid-session (via a tool call), without a new prompt being submitted.
    20→// Without this migration, checkpoints would be saved to an orphaned shadow branch.
    21→//
    22→// Returns true if migration occurred, false otherwise.
    23→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
    24→	if state == nil || state.BaseCommit == "" {
    25→		return false, nil
    26→	}
    27→
    28→	head, err := repo.Head()
    29→	if err != nil {
    30→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
    31→	}
    32→
    33→	currentHead := head.Hash().String()
    34→	if state.BaseCommit == currentHead {
    35→		return false, nil // No migration needed
    36→	}
    37→
    38→	// HEAD changed - check if old shadow branch exists and migrate it
    39→	oldShadowBranch := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
    40→	newShadowBranch := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(currentHead, state.WorktreeID)
    41→
    42→	// Guard against hash prefix collision: if both commits produce the same
    43→	// shadow branch name (same 7-char prefix), just update state - no ref rename needed
    44→	if oldShadowBranch == newShadowBranch {
    45→		state.BaseCommit = currentHead
    46→		return true, nil
    47→	}
    48→
    49→	oldRefName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(oldShadowBranch)
    50→	oldRef, err := repo.Reference(oldRefName, true)
    51→	if err != nil {
    52→		// Old shadow branch doesn't exist - just update state.BaseCommit
    53→		// This can happen if this is the first checkpoint after HEAD changed
    54→		state.BaseCommit = currentHead
    55→		logging.Info(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "migration"), "updated session base commit (HEAD changed during session)",
    56→			slog.String("new_base", currentHead[:7]))
    57→		return true, nil //nolint:nilerr // err is "reference not found" which is fine - just need to update state
    58→	}
    59→
    60→	// Old shadow branch exists - move it to new base commit
    61→	newRefName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(newShadowBranch)
    62→
    63→	// Create new reference pointing to same commit as old shadow branch
    64→	newRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(newRefName, oldRef.Hash())
    65→	if err := repo.Storer.SetReference(newRef); err != nil {
    66→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to create new shadow branch %s: %w", newShadowBranch, err)
    67→	}
    68→
    69→	// Delete old reference via CLI (go-git v5's RemoveReference doesn't persist with packed refs/worktrees)
    70→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "migration")
    71→	if err := DeleteBranchCLI(ctx, oldShadowBranch); err != nil {
    72→		// Non-fatal: log but continue - the important thing is the new branch exists
    73→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to remove old shadow branch",
    74→			slog.String("shadow_branch", oldShadowBranch),
    75→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
    76→	}
    77→
    78→	logging.Info(logCtx, "moved shadow branch (HEAD changed during session)",
    79→		slog.String("from", oldShadowBranch),
    80→		slog.String("to", newShadowBranch))
    81→
    82→	// Update state with new base commit.
    83→	// NOTE: AttributionBaseCommit is intentionally NOT updated here. Migration
    84→	// renames the shadow branch but its checkpoint trees are still relative to
    85→	// the original base. Attribution must diff from that original base to
    86→	// correctly measure agent work captured in those checkpoints.

    88→	return true, nil
    89→}

    18→type BlobFetchFunc func(ctx context.Context, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error
    19→
    20→// FetchingTree wraps a git tree to automatically fetch missing blobs on demand.
    21→// After a treeless fetch (--filter=blob:none), tree objects are available locally
    22→// but blob objects are not. Each File() call checks whether the target blob
    23→// exists locally and fetches it from the remote if missing, using FindEntry
    24→// to locate the blob hash without resolving the blob itself.
    25→//
    26→// Because go-git's ObjectStorage caches the packfile index and never refreshes
    27→// it, blobs fetched by external git commands (e.g. git fetch-pack) may not be
    28→// visible to go-git's storer. As a fallback, File() reads the blob via
    29→// "git cat-file" which always sees the current on-disk object store.
    30→//
    31→// For best performance, call PreFetch before reading files. PreFetch walks
    32→// the tree, identifies locally-missing blobs, and batch-fetches them in a
    33→// single network round-trip instead of one fetch per File() miss.
    34→type FetchingTree struct {

    41→// NewFetchingTree wraps a git tree with on-demand blob fetching.
    42→// The storer is used to check if blobs exist locally, and fetch is called
    43→// to download any that are missing. If fetch is nil, File() behaves
    44→// identically to the underlying tree.
    45→func NewFetchingTree(ctx context.Context, tree *object.Tree, s storer.EncodedObjectStorer, fetch BlobFetchFunc) *FetchingTree {
    46→	return &FetchingTree{
    47→		inner:  tree,
    48→		ctx:    ctx,
    49→		storer: s,
    50→		fetch:  fetch,
    51→	}

    54→// File returns the file at the given path. If the blob is not available
    55→// locally (e.g. after a treeless fetch), it is fetched on demand. If go-git's
    56→// storer still can't see the blob after fetching (due to cached packfile index),
    57→// the blob is read via "git cat-file" and an in-memory File is returned.
    58→func (t *FetchingTree) File(path string) (*object.File, error) {

    60→	file, err := t.inner.File(path)

   111→// PreFetch walks the tree recursively, identifies blob entries that are missing
   112→// from the local object store, and batch-fetches them in a single call to
   113→// t.fetch. This avoids per-blob network round-trips during subsequent File()
   114→// calls. It is safe to call even when all blobs are already local (no-op).
   115→// Returns the number of blobs fetched.
   116→func (t *FetchingTree) PreFetch() (int, error) {
   117→	if t.fetch == nil || t.storer == nil {
   118→		return 0, nil
   119→	}
   120→
   121→	missing := t.collectMissingBlobs(t.inner)
   122→	if len(missing) == 0 {
   123→		return 0, nil
   124→	}
   125→
   126→	logging.Debug(t.ctx, "FetchingTree.PreFetch: batch-fetching missing blobs",
   127→		slog.Int("count", len(missing)),
   128→	)
   129→
   130→	if err := t.fetch(t.ctx, missing); err != nil {
   131→		return 0, fmt.Errorf("prefetch %d blobs: %w", len(missing), err)
   132→	}
   133→
   134→	return len(missing), nil
   135→}
   136→
   137→// collectMissingBlobs recursively walks a tree and returns hashes of blob
   138→// entries that are not present in the local object store.
   139→func (t *FetchingTree) collectMissingBlobs(tree *object.Tree) []plumbing.Hash {
   140→	var missing []plumbing.Hash
   141→	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
   142→		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
   143→			if t.storer.HasEncodedObject(entry.Hash) != nil {
   144→				missing = append(missing, entry.Hash)
   145→			}
   146→		} else {
   147→			// Recurse into subtrees (tree objects are local after treeless fetch).
   148→			subtree, err := tree.Tree(entry.Name)
   149→			if err == nil {
   150→				missing = append(missing, t.collectMissingBlobs(subtree)...)
   151→			}
   152→		}
   153→	}
   154→	return missing
   155→}
   156→
   157→// readFileViaGit reads a blob via "git cat-file -p <hash>" and returns an
   158→// in-memory *object.File. This bypasses go-git's storer which may have a
   159→// stale packfile index after external git commands fetched new objects.
   160→func (t *FetchingTree) readFileViaGit(path string, entry *object.TreeEntry) (*object.File, error) {
   161→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.ctx, "git", "cat-file", "-p", entry.Hash.String())
   162→	content, cmdErr := cmd.Output()
   163→	if cmdErr != nil {
   164→		logging.Warn(t.ctx, "FetchingTree.readFileViaGit: cat-file failed",
   165→			slog.String("path", path),
   166→			slog.String("hash", entry.Hash.String()[:12]),
   167→			slog.String("error", cmdErr.Error()),
   168→		)
   169→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob %s not readable after fetch: %w", entry.Hash.String()[:12], cmdErr)
   170→	}
   171→
   172→	// Create an in-memory encoded object to construct the File.
   173→	memObj := &plumbing.MemoryObject{}
   174→	memObj.SetType(plumbing.BlobObject)
   175→	memObj.SetSize(int64(len(content)))
   176→	w, wErr := memObj.Writer()
   177→	if wErr != nil {
   178→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("memory object writer: %w", wErr)
   179→	}
   180→	if _, wErr = w.Write(content); wErr != nil {
   181→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("memory object write: %w", wErr)
   182→	}
   183→	if wErr = w.Close(); wErr != nil {
   184→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("memory object close: %w", wErr)
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	blob := &object.Blob{}
   188→	if dErr := blob.Decode(memObj); dErr != nil {
   189→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob decode: %w", dErr)
   190→	}
   191→
   192→	logging.Debug(t.ctx, "FetchingTree.readFileViaGit: blob read successfully",
   193→		slog.String("path", path),
   194→		slog.String("hash", entry.Hash.String()[:12]),
   195→		slog.Int64("size", int64(len(content))),
   196→	)
   197→
   198→	return object.NewFile(path, entry.Mode, blob), nil
   199→}

   202→// behavior.
   203→func (t *FetchingTree) Tree(path string) (*FetchingTree, error) {

    36→// UpdateSubtreeOptions configures the behavior of UpdateSubtree.

    44→
    45→// UpdateSubtree replaces or creates a subtree at the given path within an existing tree.
    46→// It walks the tree path, replacing only the entries along the modified path.
    47→// All sibling entries at each level retain their original hashes — no re-reading needed.
    48→//

    50→// newEntries are the files/dirs to place at the leaf directory.
    51→// Returns the new root tree hash.
    52→func UpdateSubtree(
    53→	repo *git.Repository,

## Comprehensive Checkpoint Package Exploration

Based on my thorough exploration of `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/`, here's what I found:

### 1. **GitStore Structure** (`store.go`)

The `GitStore` is the primary checkpoint storage implementation with minimal code:

```go
type GitStore struct {
    repo        *git.Repository
    blobFetcher BlobFetchFunc
}
```

It wraps a git repository and implements the `Store` interface, providing methods for reading/writing both temporary (shadow branch) and committed (metadata branch) checkpoints. It can optionally use a `BlobFetchFunc` to fetch missing blobs on-demand after treeless fetches.

### 2. **Core Types & Options**

**WriteCommittedOptions** - Write a checkpoint to the metadata branch with comprehensive fields:
- **Identity**: `CheckpointID`, `SessionID`, `Strategy`, `Branch`
- **Content**: `Transcript`, `Prompts`, `FilesTouched`, `CheckpointsCount`
- **Session context**: `AuthorName`, `AuthorEmail`, `EphemeralBranch`
- **Metadata**: `Agent`, `Model`, `TurnID`, `TokenUsage`, `SessionMetrics`
- **Attribution**: `InitialAttribution`, `PromptAttributionsJSON`
- **Summaries**: `Summary` (AI-generated), `CompactTranscript` (v2 format)
- **Task checkpoints**: `IsTask`, `ToolUseID`, `AgentID`, `CheckpointUUID`, `TranscriptPath`, `SubagentTranscriptPath`
- **Incremental checkpoints**: `IsIncremental`, `IncrementalSequence`, `IncrementalType`, `IncrementalData`
- **Metadata directory**: `MetadataDir` (copies all files from directory to checkpoint)

**UpdateCommittedOptions** - Update an existing checkpoint's transcript and prompts (replace semantics):
- `CheckpointID`, `SessionID`, `Transcript`, `Prompts`, `Agent`, `CompactTranscript`

**CheckpointSummary** - Root-level metadata.json for a checkpoint:
- Aggregated statistics across all sessions
- `Sessions` array mapping session IDs to file paths (`SessionFilePaths`)
- Optional: `TokenUsage`, `CombinedAttribution`

**CommittedMetadata** - Session-specific metadata.json:
- All the per-session details including `InitialAttribution` (line-level attribution at commit time)
- `CheckpointTranscriptStart` (transcript position when checkpoint started) + deprecated `TranscriptLinesAtStart`
- `PromptAttributions` (diagnostic field showing which prompt recorded which "user" lines)

### 3. **WriteCommitted Implementation** (`committed.go` lines 40-117)

The function orchestrates a 5-step process with **O(checkpoint files)** complexity via tree surgery:

1. **Validate identifiers** - Check checkpoint ID, session ID, tool use ID, agent ID for path traversal prevention
2. **Ensure sessions branch** - Creates `entire/checkpoints/v1` if missing
3. **Flatten checkpoint subtree** - Reads only the checkpoint's shard path (O(files in checkpoint), not all checkpoints)
4. **Write entries**:
   - Task checkpoints: Write incremental checkpoints or final checkpoint.json + subagent transcripts
   - Standard checkpoints: Write session files to numbered subdirectories (0/, 1/, 2/...) with metadata, transcript, prompts
5. **Splice into root** - Uses tree surgery (`UpdateSubtree`) to update only the modified shard, preserving sibling checkpoints

### 4. **Key Helper Functions**

#### **BuildTreeFromEntries** (`temporary.go` lines 977-994)
Builds a proper git tree structure from flattened file entries using a hierarchical treeNode:
```go
root := &treeNode{
    entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),  // subdirectories
    files:   []object.TreeEntry{},        // files in this directory
}
```
- Inserts all flattened paths into the structure
- Recursively builds tree objects bottom-up
- Sorts entries per git requirements (with directories having trailing "/" for sort)

#### **CreateBlobFromContent** (`committed.go` lines 1430-1456)
Creates a git blob object from in-memory byte content:
1. Creates an encoded object via `repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()`
2. Sets type to `plumbing.BlobObject` and size
3. Gets a writer and writes content
4. Stores in the storer and returns the SHA-1 hash

#### **CreateCommit** (`committed.go` lines 1601-1630)
Creates a git commit object:
1. Builds commit with tree hash, author signature (name, email, timestamp)
2. Sets parent hash (or empty for orphan commits)
3. Encodes and stores in storer
4. Returns commit hash

#### **UpdateSubtree** (`parse_tree.go` lines 45-119)
**Tree surgery** - efficiently updates a subtree by walking the path and replacing only modified entries:
- O(depth) complexity instead of O(all files)
- Siblings at each level retain their original hashes
- Two merge modes:
  - `ReplaceAll`: Replace entire leaf directory
  - `MergeKeepExisting`: Merge new entries, keeping existing ones
- Used by `spliceCheckpointSubtree` to install checkpoint tree at shard location

#### **FlattenTree** (`temporary.go` lines 775-801)
Recursively flattens a git tree into a map of full paths to entries:
- Recursively follows tree objects for directories
- Stores all files as entries with full path keys
- Used to read existing checkpoints before modification

### 5. **V2GitStore (Dual-Write Pattern)** (`v2_store.go`, `v2_committed.go`)

Separate store implementation for v2 ref layout with **dual-write to two custom refs**:

```go
type V2GitStore struct {
    repo *git.Repository
    gs   *GitStore  // Reuses entry-building helpers
    maxCheckpointsPerGeneration int
    FetchRemote string
}
```

**V2 refs**:
- `/main` (refs/entire/main): Metadata + compact transcripts (no raw full.jsonl)
- `/full/current` (refs/entire/full/current): Raw transcripts + content hash (replaces previous)

**WriteCommitted** orchestration:
1. Validate identifiers upfront
2. Write to `/main` → returns session index
3. Write to `/full/current` → uses same session index for consistency

**UpdateCommitted** (at stop time):
1. Update `/main` ref: prompts + compact transcript if provided
2. Update `/full/current` ref: raw transcript if provided
3. Keeps both refs in sync with the same session index

### 6. **Redaction Integration**

Uses the `redact` package for secrets masking:

- **redact.JSONLBytes()** - JSONL-aware redaction (handles structured logs)
- **redact.Bytes()** - Plain string redaction (fallback for invalid JSONL)
- **redact.String()** - String redaction for single values

Applied to:
- **Transcript**: JSONL-aware redaction before chunking (content hash reflects redacted content)
- **Prompts**: Joined and redacted via `redact.String(JoinPrompts(...))`
- **Subagent transcripts**: JSONL-aware with fallback to plain redaction
- **Summaries**: All text fields redacted (`Intent`, `Outcome`, `Friction`, `Learnings`, `OpenItems`, `CodeLearning.Finding`), but structure fields preserved (`Path`, `Line`, `EndLine`)
- **Metadata files from directory**: Redacted via `createRedactedBlobFromFile()` (binary files skipped, JSONL gets special handling)

### 7. **Session Structure**

Checkpoints contain **numbered subdirectories** (0-based) for multi-session support:

```
<checkpoint-id[:2]>/<checkpoint-id[2:]>/
├── metadata.json           # CheckpointSummary (root-level, aggregated)
├── 0/                      # First session (or existing session if dedup match)
│   ├── metadata.json       # CommittedMetadata (session-specific)
│   ├── full.jsonl          # Transcript (chunked if >MaxChunkSize)
│   ├── prompt.txt          # Prompts
│   └── content_hash.txt    # SHA256 of transcript
├── 1/                      # Second session
└── 2/                      # Third session...
```

**Session index determination** (via `findSessionIndex()`):
- If session ID matches existing session → reuse that index (dedup)
- Otherwise → use next available index (append)

### 8. **Checkpoint Entry Writing Functions**

#### **writeTaskCheckpointEntries** (lines 178-186)
- **Incremental**: Writes `checkpoints/NNN-<tool-use-id>.json` with redacted tool input
- **Final**: Writes `checkpoint.json` + `agent-<agent-id>.jsonl` (subagent transcript)

#### **writeStandardCheckpointEntries** (lines 289-329)
Orchestrates session file writing:
1. Read existing summary to get current session count
2. Determine session index (reuse existing or append)

   - Standard checkpoints: Write session files to numbered subdirectories (0/, 1/, 2/...) with metadata, transcript, prompts
5. **Splice into root** - Uses tree surgery (`UpdateSubtree`) to update only the modified shard, preserving sibling checkpoints

#### **BuildTreeFromEntries** (`temporary.go` lines 977-994)
Builds a proper git tree structure from flattened file entries using a hierarchical treeNode:

root := &treeNode{
    entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),  // subdirectories
    files:   []object.TreeEntry{},        // files in this directory

- Recursively builds tree objects bottom-up
- Sorts entries per git requirements (with directories having trailing "/" for sort)

#### **CreateBlobFromContent** (`committed.go` lines 1430-1456)
Creates a git blob object from in-memory byte content:

Creates a git commit object:

2. Sets parent hash (or empty for orphan commits)
3. Encodes and stores in storer
4. Returns commit hash

#### **UpdateSubtree** (`parse_tree.go` lines 45-119)
**Tree surgery** - efficiently updates a subtree by walking the path and replacing only modified entries:
- O(depth) complexity instead of O(all files)
- Siblings at each level retain their original hashes
- Two merge modes:
  - `ReplaceAll`: Replace entire leaf directory
  - `MergeKeepExisting`: Merge new entries, keeping existing ones

Recursively flattens a git tree into a map of full paths to entries:

- Stores all files as entries with full path keys
- Used to read existing checkpoints before modification

   271→	CheckpointTranscriptStart   int    // Transcript line offset at start of this checkpoint's data
   272→
   273→	// CheckpointTranscriptStart is written to both CommittedMetadata.CheckpointTranscriptStart
   274→	// and the deprecated CommittedMetadata.TranscriptLinesAtStart for backward compatibility.
   275→
   276→	// TokenUsage contains the token usage for this checkpoint
   277→	TokenUsage *agent.TokenUsage
   278→
   279→	// SessionMetrics contains hook-provided session metrics (duration, turns, context usage)
   280→	SessionMetrics *SessionMetrics
   281→
   282→	// InitialAttribution is line-level attribution calculated at commit time
   283→	// comparing checkpoint tree (agent work) to committed tree (may include human edits)
   284→	InitialAttribution *InitialAttribution
   285→
   286→	// PromptAttributionsJSON is the raw PromptAttributions data, JSON-encoded.
   287→	// Persisted for diagnostic purposes — shows exactly which prompt recorded
   288→	// which "user" lines, enabling root cause analysis of attribution bugs.
   289→	// Uses json.RawMessage to avoid importing session package.
   290→	PromptAttributionsJSON json.RawMessage
   291→
   292→	// Summary is an optional AI-generated summary for this checkpoint.
   293→	// This field may be nil when:
   294→	//   - summarization is disabled in settings
   295→	//   - summary generation failed (non-blocking, logged as warning)
   296→	//   - the transcript was empty or too short to summarize
   297→	//   - the checkpoint predates the summarization feature
   298→	Summary *Summary
   299→
   300→	// CompactTranscript is the Entire Transcript Format (transcript.jsonl) bytes.
   301→	// Written to v2 /main ref alongside metadata. May be nil if compaction
   302→	// was not performed (unknown agent, compaction error, empty transcript).
   303→	CompactTranscript []byte
   304→}
   305→
   306→// UpdateCommittedOptions contains options for updating an existing committed checkpoint.
   307→// Uses replace semantics: the transcript and prompts are fully replaced,
   308→// not appended. At stop time we have the complete session transcript and want every
   309→// checkpoint to contain it identically.
   310→type UpdateCommittedOptions struct {
   311→	// CheckpointID identifies the checkpoint to update
   312→	CheckpointID id.CheckpointID
   313→
   314→	// SessionID identifies which session slot to update within the checkpoint
   315→	SessionID string
   316→
   317→	// Transcript is the full session transcript (replaces existing)
   318→	Transcript []byte
   319→
   320→	// Prompts contains all user prompts (replaces existing)
   321→	Prompts []string
   322→
   323→	// Agent identifies the agent type (needed for transcript chunking)
   324→	Agent types.AgentType
   325→
   326→	// CompactTranscript is the updated Entire Transcript Format bytes.
   327→	// If non-nil, replaces the existing transcript.jsonl on v2 /main.
   328→	CompactTranscript []byte
   329→}

   331→// CommittedInfo contains summary information about a committed checkpoint.
   332→type CommittedInfo struct {
   333→	// CheckpointID is the stable 12-hex-char identifier
   334→	CheckpointID id.CheckpointID
   335→
   336→	// SessionID is the session identifier (most recent session for multi-session checkpoints)
   337→	SessionID string
   338→
   339→	// CreatedAt is when the checkpoint was created
   340→	CreatedAt time.Time
   341→
   342→	// CheckpointsCount is the total number of checkpoints across all sessions
   343→	CheckpointsCount int
   344→
   345→	// FilesTouched are files modified during all sessions
   346→	FilesTouched []string
   347→
   348→	// Agent identifies the agent that created this checkpoint
   349→	Agent types.AgentType
   350→
   351→	// IsTask indicates if this is a task checkpoint
   352→	IsTask bool
   353→
   354→	// ToolUseID is the tool use ID for task checkpoints
   355→	ToolUseID string
   356→
   357→	// Multi-session support
   358→	SessionCount int      // Number of sessions (1 if single session)
   359→	SessionIDs   []string // All session IDs that contributed
   360→}
   361→
   362→// SessionContent contains the actual content for a session.
   363→// This is used when reading full session data (transcript, prompts, context)
   364→// as opposed to just the metadata/summary.
   365→type SessionContent struct {
   366→	// Metadata contains the session-specific metadata
   367→	Metadata CommittedMetadata
   368→
   369→	// Transcript is the session transcript content
   370→	Transcript []byte
   371→
   372→	// Prompts contains user prompts from this session
   373→	Prompts string
   374→}

   376→// CommittedMetadata contains the metadata stored in metadata.json for each checkpoint.
   377→type CommittedMetadata struct {
   378→	CLIVersion       string          `json:"cli_version,omitempty"`
   379→	CheckpointID     id.CheckpointID `json:"checkpoint_id"`
   380→	SessionID        string          `json:"session_id"`
   381→	Strategy         string          `json:"strategy"`
   382→	CreatedAt        time.Time       `json:"created_at"`
   383→	Branch           string          `json:"branch,omitempty"` // Branch where checkpoint was created (empty if detached HEAD)
   384→	CheckpointsCount int             `json:"checkpoints_count"`
   385→	FilesTouched     []string        `json:"files_touched"`
   386→
   387→	// Agent identifies the agent that created this checkpoint (e.g., "Claude Code", "Cursor")
   388→	Agent types.AgentType `json:"agent,omitempty"`
   389→
   390→	// Model is the LLM model used during the session (e.g., "claude-sonnet-4-20250514")
   391→	Model string `json:"model,omitempty"`
   392→
   393→	// TurnID correlates checkpoints from the same agent turn.
   394→	// When a turn's work spans multiple commits, each gets its own checkpoint
   395→	// but they share the same TurnID for future aggregation/deduplication.
   396→	TurnID string `json:"turn_id,omitempty"`
   397→
   398→	// Task checkpoint fields (only populated for task checkpoints)
   399→	IsTask    bool   `json:"is_task,omitempty"`
   400→	ToolUseID string `json:"tool_use_id,omitempty"`
   401→
   402→	// Transcript position at checkpoint start - tracks what was added during this checkpoint
   403→	TranscriptIdentifierAtStart string `json:"transcript_identifier_at_start,omitempty"` // Last identifier when checkpoint started (UUID for Claude, message ID for Gemini)
   404→	CheckpointTranscriptStart   int    `json:"checkpoint_transcript_start,omitempty"`    // Transcript line offset at start of this checkpoint's data
   405→
   406→	// Deprecated: Use CheckpointTranscriptStart instead. Written for backward compatibility with older CLI versions.
   407→	TranscriptLinesAtStart int `json:"transcript_lines_at_start,omitempty"`
   408→
   409→	// Token usage for this checkpoint
   410→	TokenUsage *agent.TokenUsage `json:"token_usage,omitempty"`
   411→
   412→	// SessionMetrics contains hook-provided session metrics (duration, turns, context usage).
   413→	// Populated for agents that provide these metrics via hooks (e.g., Cursor).
   414→	SessionMetrics *SessionMetrics `json:"session_metrics,omitempty"`
   415→
   416→	// AI-generated summary of the checkpoint
   417→	Summary *Summary `json:"summary,omitempty"`
   418→
   419→	// InitialAttribution is line-level attribution calculated at commit time
   420→	InitialAttribution *InitialAttribution `json:"initial_attribution,omitempty"`
   421→
   422→	// PromptAttributions is the raw per-prompt attribution data used to compute InitialAttribution.
   423→	// Diagnostic field — shows which prompt recorded which "user" lines.
   424→	PromptAttributions json.RawMessage `json:"prompt_attributions,omitempty"`

   427→// GetTranscriptStart returns the transcript line offset at which this checkpoint's data begins.
   428→// Returns 0 for new checkpoints (start from beginning). For data written by older CLI versions,
   429→// falls back to the deprecated TranscriptLinesAtStart field.
   430→func (m CommittedMetadata) GetTranscriptStart() int {
   431→	if m.CheckpointTranscriptStart > 0 {
   432→		return m.CheckpointTranscriptStart
   433→	}
   434→	return m.TranscriptLinesAtStart
   435→}

   437→// SessionFilePaths contains the absolute paths to session files from the git tree root.
   438→// Paths include the full checkpoint path prefix (e.g., "/a1/b2c3d4e5f6/1/metadata.json").
   439→// Used in CheckpointSummary.Sessions to map session IDs to their file locations.
   440→type SessionFilePaths struct {
   441→	Metadata    string `json:"metadata"`
   442→	Transcript  string `json:"transcript,omitempty"`
   443→	ContentHash string `json:"content_hash,omitempty"`
   444→	Prompt      string `json:"prompt"`
   445→}
   446→
   447→// CheckpointSummary is the root-level metadata.json for a checkpoint.
   448→// It contains aggregated statistics from all sessions and a map of session IDs
   449→// to their file paths. Session-specific data (including initial_attribution)
   450→// is stored in the session's subdirectory metadata.json.
   451→//
   452→// Structure on entire/checkpoints/v1 branch:
   453→//
   454→//	<checkpoint-id[:2]>/<checkpoint-id[2:]>/
   455→//	├── metadata.json         # This CheckpointSummary
   456→//	├── 1/                    # First session
   457→//	│   ├── metadata.json     # Session-specific CommittedMetadata
   458→//	│   ├── full.jsonl
   459→//	│   ├── prompt.txt
   460→//	│   └── content_hash.txt
   461→//	├── 2/                    # Second session
   462→//	└── 3/                    # Third session...
   463→//
   464→//nolint:revive // Named CheckpointSummary to avoid conflict with existing Summary struct
   465→type CheckpointSummary struct {
   466→	CLIVersion          string              `json:"cli_version,omitempty"`
   467→	CheckpointID        id.CheckpointID     `json:"checkpoint_id"`
   468→	Strategy            string              `json:"strategy"`
   469→	Branch              string              `json:"branch,omitempty"`
   470→	CheckpointsCount    int                 `json:"checkpoints_count"`
   471→	FilesTouched        []string            `json:"files_touched"`
   472→	Sessions            []SessionFilePaths  `json:"sessions"`
   473→	TokenUsage          *agent.TokenUsage   `json:"token_usage,omitempty"`
   474→	CombinedAttribution *InitialAttribution `json:"combined_attribution,omitempty"`
   475→}
   476→
   477→// SessionMetrics contains hook-provided session metrics from agents that report
   478→// them via lifecycle hooks (e.g., Cursor). These supplement transcript-derived
   479→// metrics for agents whose transcripts lack usage/timing data.
   480→type SessionMetrics struct {
   481→	DurationMs        int64 `json:"duration_ms,omitempty"`
   482→	TurnCount         int   `json:"turn_count,omitempty"`
   483→	ContextTokens     int   `json:"context_tokens,omitempty"`
   484→	ContextWindowSize int   `json:"context_window_size,omitempty"`
   485→}
   486→
   487→// Summary contains AI-generated summary of a checkpoint.
   488→type Summary struct {
   489→	Intent    string           `json:"intent"`     // What user wanted to accomplish
   490→	Outcome   string           `json:"outcome"`    // What was achieved
   491→	Learnings LearningsSummary `json:"learnings"`  // Categorized learnings
   492→	Friction  []string         `json:"friction"`   // Problems/annoyances encountered
   493→	OpenItems []string         `json:"open_items"` // Tech debt, unfinished work
   494→}
   495→
   496→// LearningsSummary contains learnings grouped by scope.
   497→type LearningsSummary struct {
   498→	Repo     []string       `json:"repo"`     // Codebase-specific patterns/conventions
   499→	Code     []CodeLearning `json:"code"`     // File/module specific findings
   500→	Workflow []string       `json:"workflow"` // General dev practices
   501→}
   502→
   503→// CodeLearning captures a learning tied to a specific code location.
   504→type CodeLearning struct {
   505→	Path    string `json:"path"`               // File path
   506→	Line    int    `json:"line,omitempty"`     // Start line number
   507→	EndLine int    `json:"end_line,omitempty"` // End line for ranges (optional)
   508→	Finding string `json:"finding"`            // What was learned
   509→}
   510→
   511→// InitialAttribution captures line-level attribution metrics at commit time.
   512→// This is a point-in-time snapshot comparing the checkpoint tree (agent work)
   513→// against the committed tree (may include human edits).
   514→//
   515→// Attribution Metrics:
   516→//   - TotalCommitted keeps the historical "net additions" view for compatibility
   517→//   - TotalLinesChanged measures total committed line changes (adds + modifies + removes)
   518→//   - AgentPercentage represents "of the lines changed in this commit, what percentage came from the agent"
   519→//   - AgentRemoved tracks committed deletions performed by the agent
   520→type InitialAttribution struct {
   521→	CalculatedAt      time.Time `json:"calculated_at"`
   522→	AgentLines        int       `json:"agent_lines"`              // Lines added by agent that remain in the commit
   523→	AgentRemoved      int       `json:"agent_removed"`            // Lines removed by agent that remain removed in the commit
   524→	HumanAdded        int       `json:"human_added"`              // Lines added by human (excluding modifications)
   525→	HumanModified     int       `json:"human_modified"`           // Lines modified by human (estimate: min(added, removed))
   526→	HumanRemoved      int       `json:"human_removed"`            // Lines removed by human (excluding modifications)
   527→	TotalCommitted    int       `json:"total_committed"`          // Net additions in commit (legacy additions-focused metric)
   528→	TotalLinesChanged int       `json:"total_lines_changed"`      // Total committed line changes (adds + modifies + removes)
   529→	AgentPercentage   float64   `json:"agent_percentage"`         // (agent_lines + agent_removed) / total_lines_changed * 100
   530→	MetricVersion     int       `json:"metric_version,omitempty"` // 0/absent = legacy (additions-only %), 2 = changed-lines %
   531→}

   538→

   540→	SessionID string
   541→

# git metadata project

This is a proposed specification for a new standardized way to attach and exchange arbitrary metadata in Git projects.

## Why this project exists

> [!YOUTUBE]
> https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=46bV6KT0SsQ&REDACTED&index=4
> Rodrigo Bovendorp's metadata talk at JJCon 2025, outlining the overall problem set this project is meant to address.

This is a proposal to provide a more flexible and scalable metadata system for Git projects than the tools Git commonly uses today such as `git notes`, commit headers, message trailers, and checked-in helper files like `CODEOWNERS`.

### Limitations of Current Solutions

These existing approaches tend to have some important limitations:

- limited control over metadata granularity and mutability
- poor support for many independently addressable fields on the same object
- awkward merge behavior for structured data
- file pollution when metadata has to live in the working tree
- poor scaling characteristics for very large metadata sets

### Metadata Use Cases

This project is meant to more elagantly support a wider variety of metadata use cases such as:

- provenance for generated code, prompts, and transcripts
- trust and review information
- comments and review discussions
- testing results and attestations
- path- or project-scoped metadata like ownership or policy hints

### Overall Goals

The core idea is to:

- support more fine grained metadata targets (branches, paths, etc)
- store metadata locally in a format that is fast to query and mutate
- exchange metadata using normal Git trees, commits, refs, and transport mechanisms
- model mergeable data as many small tree entries instead of large structured blobs

That combination is meant to make metadata:

- easy to read and write locally
- exchangeable over existing Git hosting infrastructure
- eventually consistent across collaborators
- practical even when metadata grows large

## Approach

This project has two parts. One is specifying an agreed upon exchange format that accomplishes these goals. The other is a local reference implementation that can be used, referenced or built upon.

## Exchange format

The important part is the exchange format - how metadata is stored, transmitted and updated among teams working on a project. This is what would need to be agreed upon for wider interop.

We refer to this as "serialization" - how to write data into Git primiatives for exchange, and "materialization" - how to update local values when receiving new data.

- [Targets and keys](./exchange-format/targets.md)
- [Exchange format and refs](./exchange-format/exchange.md)
- [Materialization and merge workflow](./exchange-format/materialization.md)

### Value types

There are three initial data types that can be used for any given target key. Here are the specifications for how those data types are serialized.

# Serialization

This document describes how to serialize metadata into Git primatives that can be transferred via normal Git remote protocols.

[Interactive demo of the serialization format](../other/example-serialize.html)

## Commit model

Serialization writes a Git commit whose tree contains the current shareable metadata state.

- tree pointer
- author identity
- author date / commit date
- ancestry for incremental materialization and merging

## Tree root layout

The base tree path for a target is target-type dependent:

- `commit` → `<target-type>/<first2-of-sha>/<full-target-value>`
- `branch` / `change-id` → `<target-type>/<fanout>/<full-target-value>`
- `path` → `path/<escaped path segments...>/__target__`
- `project` → `project`

Fanout is target-type dependent:

- for `commit`, use the first 2 characters of the commit SHA
- for `path`, do not hash the target value; serialize the path segments directly
- for anything else (`branch`, `change-id`), use the first 2 hexadecimal characters of the SHA-1 hash of the target value (ie, the branch name or change-id value)

Examples:

- `commit/13/13a7d29cde8f8557b54fd6474f547a56822180ae/...`
- `branch/06/sc-branch-1-deadbeef/...`
- `path/src/metrics/__target__/owner/__value`

For `path` targets, a reserved separator component `__target__` marks the end of the target path and the beginning of key segments.
If a serialized path segment would begin with `__`, it must be escaped by prefixing it with `~`.
To keep this reversible, a path segment beginning with `~` should also be escaped by prefixing it with `~`.
Examples:

- raw path segment `__generated` → serialized as `~__generated`
- raw path segment `~scratch` → serialized as `~~scratch`

This keeps commit paths readable, preserves human-readable path targets, and still avoids ambiguity between serialized path targets and metadata structure.

## Key path layout

Under the target base path, key segments are serialized directly as path components.

Metadata structure begins when a reserved `__*` component is encountered.

Examples:

- string: `<base>/agent/model/__value`
- list: `<base>/agent/chat/__list/<entry-id>`
- whole-key tombstone: `<base>/__tombstones/agent/model/__deleted`

## Per-type layouts

Per-type layouts are defined in:

- [Strings](./strings.md)
- [Lists](./lists.md)
- [Sets](./sets.md)

## Key path reservation

Keys are serialized directly under the target base path.

Any path component beginning with `__` is reserved for gmeta structural paths such as:

- `__value`
- `__list`
- `__set`
- `__tombstones`
- `__target__` (used only as the separator inside serialized `path` targets)

This means user keys occupy normal path segments and metadata structure begins when a reserved `__*` path component is encountered.

## Path target encoding

`path` targets are serialized using their raw path segments rather than a hash-derived fanout prefix.

Shape:

`path/<escaped path segments...>/__target__/...`

Rules:

- each `/`-separated path component becomes one tree path component
- `__target__` marks the end of the target path and the beginning of key segments
- if a path segment begins with `__`, escape it by prefixing the segment with `~`
- if a path segment begins with `~`, also escape it by prefixing the segment with `~`

Examples:

- `path:src/metrics` → `path/src/metrics/__target__/...`
- `path:src/__generated/file.rs` → `path/src/~__generated/file.rs/__target__/...`
- `path:src/~scratch/file.rs` → `path/src/~~scratch/file.rs/__target__/...`

## Explicit deletion

Exchange must not assume that missing paths mean deletion.

Reasons:

- sparse or pruned trees may omit data
- multiple metadata refs may represent different subsets
- absence should not be ambiguous

Intentional deletion is represented by explicit tombstones.

A single reserved `__tombstones` namespace is used for both whole-key and child-level deletions. Child tombstones are interpreted relative to the current key type. Serialize and materialize must ignore incompatible child tombstones for the current type rather than treating them as errors or as deletions for another collection model.

# Strings

Strings are the simplest gmeta value type.

A string represents one current scalar value for a `(target, key)` pair.

Examples:

- `agent:model = claude-4.6`
- `owner = schacon`
- `review:signoff = schacon@gmail.com`

## Summary

- One current value per key
- Serialized as a single terminal blob
- Removal uses a key tombstone
- Concurrent updates resolve by last-writer-wins

## Serialized tree shape

For a string value, write the string to:

`[base]/<key segments>/__value`

Examples:

- `commit/13/<full-target>/agent/model/__value`
- `path/src/metrics/__target__/owner/__value`

The blob contents are the raw string value.

## Tombstones

If a string key is removed, serialize a tombstone at:

`[base]/__tombstones/<key segments>/__deleted`

The tombstone blob should be the same blob as the `__value` was. This way Git reuses the blob and we can do content comparisons if needed in cases of conflict.

When a string is set again after deletion, the tombstone is cleared locally and omitted from the next serialization.

## Merge semantics

Merging trees can technically use either `ours` or `theirs` strategies, but one value should win out. Projects or individuals can determine which they prefer.

The default in our implementation is `ours`, so that both values are in the history and reverting is possible.

# Lists

Lists in gmeta are append-friendly multi-value collections.

They are best thought of as an ordered append log of string entries, not as a general-purpose mutable array.

Examples:

- agent transcript jsonl chunks
- review comments
- a sequence of notes appended over time

## Intended semantics

The current list design is optimized for the most common concurrent operation: one or more users append new values to the same logical list.

We serialize lists as many small blobs rather than one JSON array blob so we can use normal Git tree merging tooling to avoid array-level conflicts.

## Serialized tree shape

For a list value, entries are written under:

`[base]/<key segments>/__list/<entry-id>`

Where `<entry-id>` is of the form:

`<timestamp-ms>-<content-hash-prefix>`

Examples:

- `branch/06/sc-branch-1-deadbeef/agent/chat/__list/1771232450203-23c0f`
- `path/src/metrics/__target__/comments/__list/1771232450203-23c0f`

Each blob contains one string entry.

If multiple values are inserted in one command, start from one base millisecond timestamp and increment by 1 for each additional entry so local order is preserved.

## Ordering

List order is defined by sorting `<entry-id>` lexically, which is equivalent to sorting by:

1. timestamp ascending
2. hash suffix as a stable tie-breaker

This gives deterministic ordering after merges.

## Duplicate values

Lists allow duplicate string values.

If the same text is appended twice at different times, both entries remain.

This is intentional and differentiates lists from sets.

## Tombstones

### Whole-key removal

If the entire list key is removed, write a tombstone at:

`[base]/__tombstones/<key segments>/__deleted`

This means the logical list key has been removed.

### Entry removal

Removing individual entries in a list after the fact can be done by adding a tombstone to individual entry ids.

`[base]/<key segments>/__tombstones/<entry-id>/__deleted`

Where the `__deleted` blob is the original contents of the entry.

Because `__tombstones` is shared across collection types, serialize and materialize must ignore incompatible child tombstones for the current key type. For example, if a key currently materializes as a list, only tombstones that are valid list entry identifiers should affect the visible list state; incompatible child tombstones should be preserved but ignored.

# Sets

Sets are unordered collections of unique string members.

Unlike lists:

- order does not matter
- you cannot have duplicate values

Examples:

- labels
- code owners
- capabilities or feature flags

## Serialized tree shape

For a set key, store members under:

`[base]/<key segments>/__set`

Where `__set` is a tree of the values where the tree entry name is the SHA1 of the value.

Example:

`path/src/metrics/__target__/owners/__set`

So the `__set` entry might look something like this:

```
❯ git cat-file -p meta/local:path/src/metrics/__target__/owners/__set
100644 blob 0dd8[...]4b1b2a    0dd8[...]4b1b2a
100644 blob 1296[...]a463c7    1296[...]a463c7
```

Notice that the tree entry blob sha is the same as the tree entry name.

## Member tombstones

If a member is removed from the set, write:

`[base]/<key segments>/__tombstones/<member-sha>`

with contents of the deleted entry as the tree entry value.

## Whole-key tombstones

If the entire set key is removed, also support:

`[base]/__tombstones/<key segments>/__deleted`

This deletes the logical collection itself, not just one member. The tree of `__deleted` should be what `__set` was when it was deleted.

func TestMigrateCheckpointsV2_BackfillCompactTranscript(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	repo := initMigrateTestRepo(t)
	v1Store, v2Store := newMigrateStores(repo)

	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("aabb11223344")

	// Write v1 checkpoint with agent type (so compaction can succeed)
	err := v1Store.WriteCommitted(context.Background(), checkpoint.WriteCommittedOptions{
		CheckpointID: cpID,
		SessionID:    "session-backfill",
		Strategy:     "manual-commit",
		Transcript:   []byte("{\"type\":\"user\",\"message\":{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hello\"}}\n{\"type\":\"assistant\",\"message\":{\"role\":\"assistant\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"hi\"}]}}\n"),
		Prompts:      []string{"hello"},
		Agent:        "Claude Code",
		AuthorName:   "Test",
		AuthorEmail:  "test@test.com",
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Write to v2 WITHOUT compact transcript (simulating earlier migration)
	err = v2Store.WriteCommitted(context.Background(), checkpoint.WriteCommittedOptions{
		CheckpointID: cpID,
		SessionID:    "session-backfill",
		Strategy:     "manual-commit",
		Transcript:   []byte("{\"type\":\"user\",\"message\":{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hello\"}}\n"),
		Prompts:      []string{"hello"},
		Agent:        "Claude Code",
		AuthorName:   "Test",
		AuthorEmail:  "test@test.com",
		// CompactTranscript intentionally nil
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify no transcript.jsonl on /main yet
	summary, err := v2Store.ReadCommitted(context.Background(), cpID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, summary)
	assert.Empty(t, summary.Sessions[0].Transcript, "should have no compact transcript before backfill")

	// Run migration — should backfill the compact transcript
	var stdout bytes.Buffer
	result, migrateErr := migrateCheckpointsV2(context.Background(), repo, v1Store, v2Store, &stdout)
	require.NoError(t, migrateErr)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, result.migrated, "backfill should count as migrated")
	assert.Equal(t, 0, result.skipped)
	assert.Contains(t, stdout.String(), "added transcript.jsonl")

	// Verify transcript.jsonl now exists
	summary2, err := v2Store.ReadCommitted(context.Background(), cpID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, summary2)
	assert.NotEmpty(t, summary2.Sessions[0].Transcript, "should have compact transcript after backfill")
}

func TestMigrateCheckpointsV2_RepairsCurrentFullEvenWhenArchiveExists(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	repo := initMigrateTestRepo(t)
	v1Store, v2Store := newMigrateStores(repo)

	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("334455ddeeff")
	writeV1Checkpoint(t, v1Store, cpID, "session-repair-archive-001",
		[]byte("{\"type\":\"assistant\",\"message\":\"repair from archive fallback\"}\n"),
		[]string{"repair archive prompt"},
	)

	// Initial migration to seed v2.
	var initialRun bytes.Buffer
	result1, err := migrateCheckpointsV2(context.Background(), repo, v1Store, v2Store, &initialRun)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, result1.migrated)

	// Preserve current generation as an archived ref to simulate fallback availability.
	currentCommitHash, _, refErr := v2Store.GetRefState(plumbing.ReferenceName(paths.V2FullCurrentRefName))
	require.NoError(t, refErr)
	archiveRef := plumbing.ReferenceName(paths.V2FullRefPrefix + "0000000000001")
	require.NoError(t, repo.Storer.SetReference(plumbing.NewHashReference(archiveRef, currentCommitHash)))

	// Remove current /full/current transcript artifacts.
	removeV2SessionTranscriptFiles(t, repo, v2Store, cpID, 0)

	// Sanity-check fallback exists: ReadSessionContent can still read from archive.
	archivedRead, archivedReadErr := v2Store.ReadSessionContent(context.Background(), cpID, 0)
	require.NoError(t, archivedReadErr)
	assert.NotEmpty(t, archivedRead.Transcript)

	// Re-run migration: should still repair /full/current.
	var rerun bytes.Buffer
	result2, rerunErr := migrateCheckpointsV2(context.Background(), repo, v1Store, v2Store, &rerun)
	require.NoError(t, rerunErr)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, result2.migrated)
	assert.Contains(t, rerun.String(), "repaired partial v2 checkpoint state")

	ok, checkErr := hasCurrentFullSessionArtifacts(repo, v2Store, cpID, 0)
	require.NoError(t, checkErr)
	assert.True(t, ok, "expected /full/current artifacts to be restored")
}

func removeV2SessionTranscriptFiles(t *testing.T, repo *git.Repository, v2Store *checkpoint.V2GitStore, cpID id.CheckpointID, sessionIdx int) {
	t.Helper()

	refName := plumbing.ReferenceName(paths.V2FullCurrentRefName)
	parentHash, rootTreeHash, err := v2Store.GetRefState(refName)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	newRootHash, updateErr := checkpoint.UpdateSubtree(
		repo,
		rootTreeHash,
		[]string{string(cpID[:2]), string(cpID[2:]), strconv.Itoa(sessionIdx)},
		nil,
		checkpoint.UpdateSubtreeOptions{
			MergeMode: checkpoint.MergeKeepExisting,
			DeleteNames: []string{
				paths.TranscriptFileName,
				paths.TranscriptFileName + ".001",
				paths.TranscriptFileName + ".002",
				paths.ContentHashFileName,
			},
		},
	)
	require.NoError(t, updateErr)

	commitHash, commitErr := checkpoint.CreateCommit(repo, newRootHash, parentHash, "test: remove full transcript\n", "Test", "test@test.com")
	require.NoError(t, commitErr)
	require.NoError(t, repo.Storer.SetReference(plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, commitHash)))
}

		SessionID:    "session-001",

	_, err = tree.Tree(gmetaTargetPath(cpID2))
	assert.NoError(t, err, "second checkpoint should exist")
}

// flattenTreeToStrings recursively flattens a tree into a map of path -> blob content.
func flattenTreeToStrings(t *testing.T, repo interface{ BlobObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Blob, error); TreeObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Tree, error) }, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, out map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
		path := entry.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			path = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
		}

		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
			blob, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read blob at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			reader, err := blob.Reader()
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to get reader at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			content := make([]byte, blob.Size)
			_, _ = reader.Read(content)
			_ = reader.Close()
			out[path] = string(content)
		} else {
			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read subtree at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, subtree, path, out)
		}
	}
}

// flattenTreeToStrings recursively flattens a tree into a map of path -> blob content.
func flattenTreeToStrings(t *testing.T, repo interface{ BlobObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Blob, error); TreeObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Tree, error) }, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, out map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
		path := entry.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			path = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
		}

		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
			blob, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read blob at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			reader, err := blob.Reader()
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to get reader at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			content := make([]byte, blob.Size)
			_, _ = reader.Read(content)
			_ = reader.Close()
			out[path] = string(content)
		} else {
			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read subtree at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, subtree, path, out)
		}
	}
}

	err := store.WriteCommitted(ctx, WriteCommittedOptions{

		SessionID:        "session-001",
		Strategy:         "manual-commit",
		Branch:           "main",
		Transcript:       []byte(`{"type":"text","content":"hello"}`),
		Prompts:          []string{"build a feature"},
		FilesTouched:     []string{"src/foo.go", "src/bar.go"},
		CheckpointsCount: 3,
		AuthorName:       "Test",
		AuthorEmail:      "test@test.com",
		Agent:            types.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		Model:            "claude-opus-4-6",
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify ref exists
	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName(GmetaRefName), true)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the tree and verify structure
	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	require.NoError(t, err)

	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify the target path exists: change-id/<fanout>/<checkpoint-id>/
	targetPath := gmetaTargetPath(cpID)
	targetTree, err := tree.Tree(targetPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	entries := make(map[string]string)
	flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, targetTree, "", entries)

	// Check checkpoint-level fields
	assert.Equal(t, "manual-commit", entries["entire/strategy/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "main", entries["entire/branch/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "3", entries["entire/checkpoints-count/__value"])
	assert.NotEmpty(t, entries["entire/cli-version/__value"])

	// Check files-touched set entries exist (2 files)
	setCount := 0
	for key := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(key, "entire/files-touched/__set/") {
			setCount++
		}
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 2, setCount, "expected 2 files-touched set entries")

	// Check session agent info
	assert.Equal(t, string(types.AgentTypeClaudeCode), entries["session/session-001/agent/name/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "claude-opus-4-6", entries["session/session-001/agent/model/__value"])

	// Check prompt
	assert.Equal(t, "build a feature", entries["session/session-001/prompt/__value"])

	// Check transcript list has entries
	transcriptCount := 0
	for key := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(key, "session/session-001/transcript/__list/") {
			transcriptCount++

// flattenTreeToStrings recursively flattens a tree into a map of path -> blob content.
func flattenTreeToStrings(t *testing.T, repo interface{ BlobObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Blob, error); TreeObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Tree, error) }, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, out map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
		path := entry.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			path = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
		}

		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
			blob, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read blob at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			reader, err := blob.Reader()
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to get reader at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			content := make([]byte, blob.Size)
			_, _ = reader.Read(content)
			_ = reader.Close()
			out[path] = string(content)
		} else {
			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read subtree at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, subtree, path, out)
		}
	}
}

// flattenTreeToStrings recursively flattens a tree into a map of path -> blob content.
func flattenTreeToStrings(t *testing.T, repo interface{ BlobObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Blob, error); TreeObject(plumbing.Hash) (*object.Tree, error) }, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, out map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
		path := entry.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			path = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
		}

		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
			blob, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read blob at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			reader, err := blob.Reader()
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to get reader at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			content := make([]byte, blob.Size)
			_, _ = reader.Read(content)
			_ = reader.Close()
			out[path] = string(content)
		} else {
			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read subtree at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, subtree, path, out)
		}
	}
}

### New files
- **`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go`** (~330 lines) — `GmetaStore` with `WriteCommitted` and `UpdateCommitted` methods implementing the gmeta exchange format tree layout

- **`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`** — Added `IsGmetaEnabled()` method and package-level convenience function, gated by `strategy_options.gmeta: true`

- **`cmd/entire/cli/migrate_test.go`** — Updated call signatures for new gmeta parameter

### Key design decisions
- **SHA-1 fanout** per gmeta spec: `change-id/<sha1(checkpoint-id)[:2]>/<checkpoint-id>/`
